source.title: Why flatness does and does not correlate with generalization for deep neural networks
source.authors: Shuo Zhang; Isaac Reid; Guillermo Valle Pérez; A. Louis

record.tranche_reason: Tests how generalization changes when incorrectly labeled attack examples are added, using a different setup from completely random relabeling of the training set.
record.gate_note: The paper trains on the original set plus an incorrectly labeled attack set, with attack-set size ranging from 0 to the size of the original training set. It reports results for this setup, not for completely random relabeling of the original training images. Cited findings from other studies are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study uses incorrectly labeled attack examples to generate functions with different generalization performance, then evaluates flatness and Bayesian-prior predictors. It does not establish that attack labels are completely random or measure any version's specified random-label behavior. Zero error is explicitly guaranteed on the clean set S; this alone does not establish memorization of S+A.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: local flatness can correlate with generalization, but optimizer changes and parameter rescaling can break that correlation. The authors find log P(f) a more robust predictor in their experiments, while acknowledging that its theoretical explanation and computational approximation need further work.
record.recipe_differences: Uses an added incorrectly labeled attack set to vary generalization while retaining zero error on the original set; it does not randomly relabel the full training set as in the original sources.
record.method_sensitivity: Generalization-flatness correlation varies by optimizer and architecture; ResNet50 with Adam is less degraded than FCN on MNIST. ResNet50 with Adam is difficult to fit at larger attack-set sizes.

fits_no_version.finding: Adding more incorrectly labeled attack examples worsens test generalization while preserving zero error on clean S.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Incorrectly labeled auxiliary training examples can degrade generalization while models continue to interpolate the clean training subset.

fits_no_version.finding: ResNet50 with Adam was difficult to train to zero error when the attack set exceeded 2500 examples; only smaller attack sets were displayed.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Interpolation in attack-set experiments can depend on architecture, optimizer, and attack-set size.

record.problems: The relevant label-noise-like experiment uses an added attack set rather than complete random relabeling of the original training set. The claim-relevant generalization values are mainly figure-only. ResNet50 with Adam does not reach zero training error reliably at larger attack-set sizes, and those settings are omitted.
record.rows_left_out: No claim-relevant rows omitted. Flatness, prior, and optimizer comparisons are outside the versions' stated behaviors and were not extracted as rows.

untested.parts: Completely random labeling, near-zero error on those labels, chance test performance, and unchanged architecture and hyperparameters.
Training-time comparisons between true and random labels and convergence time as corruption increases.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Perfect fitting and steady test-error degradation under randomly corrupted labels from zero to complete corruption.
Effects of weight decay, dropout, and data augmentation on random-label fitting and true-label generalization.
Relative learning trajectories for real patterns and noisy or random labels.

record.verdict_notes: Missing portions of a claim are untested, not evidence for limits_scope. Incorrect labels in a binary task need not be independent random labels. With |A|≤|S|, the attack examples constitute at most half of S+A. The paper's statement about less deterioration for ResNet50 concerns the flatness–generalization correlation, not a demonstrated smaller degradation in generalization itself.

versions.untested_parts: Does not replace all training labels with completely random labels; does not report test error at chance for this setup.
Attack-set size ranges from zero to the size of the original training set, not from zero to all training examples corrupted; the text does not report a steady rise or reaching chance.
